answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond that only unlocks after a slow work history — a tide of completed jobs that gradually raises its trust limit. Like quartz forming under pressure over time, reputation cannot be bought instantly: new identities start with tiny spending caps, and a glacier-slow escalation means an attacker must sustain many costly, well-behaved identities for months before any one can move real value. Sybil creation stays cheap, but Sybil influence becomes expensive, slow, and forfeitable when cheating is proven.
